chunks: From him, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Sulaymān ibn Jaʿfar al-Jaʿfarī, who said:

I became ill until my flesh wasted away. Then I entered upon al-Riḍā عليه السلام, and he said: “Would it please you that your flesh return to you?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Keep to the bathhouse every other day, for it will restore your flesh to you; and beware of making it habitual constantly, for constant use of it causes consumption.”

key_terms.إِدْمَانَهُ: constant habitual use of it; persistent and excessive repetition
key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the Imam giving the guidance
key_terms.الْحَمَّامَ: the bathhouse; a therapeutic public bath in the context of the narration
key_terms.غِبًّا: every other day; indicating moderated, intermittent practice
key_terms.لَحْمِي: my flesh; refers to bodily mass or physical strength lost through illness
key_terms.مَرِضْتُ: I became ill; indicates the narrator’s physical sickness

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام advise for restoring strength after illness?
ai.summary: This hadith relates practical guidance from Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام regarding bodily weakness and recovery. He advises moderate use of the bathhouse as beneficial, while warning against excessive and continuous use because of its harmful effects.
